message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference calendar showing **all “long‑weekend” occasions** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A *long weekend* here means a statutory holiday that either lands on a Friday or a Monday (or is officially moved to one of those days because it falls on a weekend). When the holiday sits between Saturday–Sunday and the following Monday, the whole stretch counts as a single extended break.

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day (Observed Mon Jan 2) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so the next working day (Mon Jan 2) became the official holiday. |
| **Apr 7–8** | Good Friday | Good Friday itself is a statutory holiday; the following Saturday gives a 2‑day break. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Last Monday before May 25. Gives a full weekend plus Monday. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (Observed Mon Jul 3) | Canada Day landed on Saturday, so the observance shifted to Monday, creating a 3‑day weekend. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | First Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 8–10** | Remembrance Day | Observed on Monday, Nov 10 (the actual day—Nov 11—is a Tuesday). |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas | Christmas Day fell on Monday, giving a 3‑day weekend (including the preceding Saturday). |

### Provincial / Territorial Variations  

Some provinces/territories celebrate additional holidays that also generate long weekends. Below are the most common ones that were relevant in 2023:

| Province/Territory | Holiday | Dates (2023) | Long‑Weekend Effect |
|--------------------|----------|--------------|---------------------|
| Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba | **Family Day** | Feb 20 (third Monday in February) | Feb 18–20 |
| Ontario | **St. George’s Day** (not a statutory holiday) | — | — |
| Quebec | **Saint‑Jean-Baptiste Day** | Jun 24 (Thursday) | None (falls mid‑week) |
| Newfoundland & Labrador | **Mawson’s Birthday** | Aug 17 (Wednesday) | None |
| Yukon | **Yukon Day** | Aug 21 (Sunday) → observed Mon Aug 28 | Aug 29–31 (if counted) |
| Nunavut | **Nunavut Day** | June 30 (Wednesday) | None |
| Northwest Territories | **NWT Day** | August 27 (Monday) | Aug 25–27 |

> **Tip:** If your application needs province‑specific calendars, consider pulling each jurisdiction’s statutory holiday schedule separately. Many open‑source datasets (e.g., GitHub repos maintained by civic tech groups) already contain up‑to‑date lists of Canadian holidays broken down by region.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the same breakdown for another year—or if you want help formatting this data for integration into your app!

Long weekends typically include statutory holidays that fall on Friday or Monday (or sometimes Thursday/Tuesday). For Canada, federal holidays:

- New Year's Day – Jan 1
- Family Day (various provinces) – third Monday Feb
- Good Friday – variable
- Victoria Day – last Monday before May 25
- Canada Day – July 1
- Labour Day – first Monday September
- Thanksgiving – second Monday October
- Remembrance Day – Nov 11 (observed if falls on weekday)
- Christmas – Dec 25
- Boxing Day – Dec 26

But some provinces also have other holidays e.g., St. Patrick's day etc. Long weekends would be those where holiday falls on Fri/Monday or adjacent days create extended weekend.

We could produce a table with dates and note which ones form long weekends.

Canada Day - July 1 (Saturday), but since it's Saturday, observe on Monday Jul 3?
